data.narrative:
Quantum Machines is a Series C quantum computing company that has raised $280M to date. The valuation analysis draws from a comp universe of 11 entities across quantum computing—three public companies (IonQ, Rigetti, D-Wave) and eight private firms including Quantinuum and Infleqtion—though the private peer set lacks sufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage comparables for a robust median-peer method.

Stage-progression analysis, the only reliably applicable triangulation method, uses the $280M total raised as a proxy base value and applies a 1.7x step-up multiplier typical of Series C-to-next-stage advancement. This yields an implied valuation of $476M. The method is grounded in the observed progression patterns across late-stage financings in the quantum sector, though the scarcity of transaction-level data for narrowly comparable private rounds introduces execution risk to the multiplier assumption.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $405M to $547M, centered on $476M. This range reflects ±15% sensitivity around the stage-progression midpoint to account for variance in round-sizing and capital efficiency. Key uncertainties include the lack of recently closed Series C comparables in quantum computing with disclosed post-money valuations, limiting calibration of the 1.7x step-up to the specific risk and stage dynamics of Quantum Machines' financing environment. Revenue, profitability trajectory, and customer concentration data would materially refine this estimate.
